q: How much is the Amazon referral fee?
a: For each item sold, Amazon charges a percentage of the total price or a per-item minimum, whichever is greater. The rate depends on the category: Everything Else, for example, is 15% with a $0.30 minimum.

q: How much does Walmart charge sellers?
a: Walmart deducts a referral fee only once you complete a sale, and says there are no setup or monthly fees. The rate is set by category; the Everything Else rate is 15%, charged on the total sales price including shipping.

q: How much does eBay take per sale?
a: In most categories without a Store, eBay charges a 13.6% final value fee on the total amount of the sale up to $7,500, calculated per item, plus a per-order fee of $0.30 on orders of $10 or less and $0.40 on larger orders. The total amount of the sale includes the item price, handling charges, shipping paid by the buyer (with some exceptions) and sales tax.

q: How much does Etsy take per sale?
a: Etsy charges a $0.20 listing fee per item and a 6.5% transaction fee on the item price plus the shipping and gift wrap you charge. For a seller whose bank account is in the US, payment processing is 3% + $0.25 on the gross order amount, including shipping and tax. Offsite Ads, when an order is attributed to them, add 15%, or 12% once a shop has $10,000 or more in sales over the prior 365 days, capped at $100 per order.

q: How much does Shopify take per sale?
a: With Shopify Payments, the standard online card rate is 2.9% + 30¢ on the Basic plan, falling to 2.25% + 30¢ on Plus. If you use a third-party payment provider instead, Shopify transaction fees of 2% on Basic down to 0.2% on Plus may apply. The plan itself is a separate monthly price, from $39/mo for Basic billed monthly.

q: What is the current merchandise processing fee?
a: Formal entries pay 0.3464% of the merchandise value. For fiscal year 2027 the fee is at least $34.58 and at most $670.86 per formal entry; an automated informal entry not prepared by CBP personnel pays a flat $2.77.

q: What is an HTS code used for?
a: It classifies an imported good. Duty rates are set at the 8-digit level, and the full 10-digit number, with its statistical suffix, goes on the entry. Exports use Schedule B instead.
